title: Continuity of Ext out of integral constructible complexes
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, regarded as a condensed coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and its bounded constructible subcategory $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of complexes of $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-modules for which there is $b\in\mathbf Z$ with $K_i^r=0$ whenever $r<b$, for every $i$. Write $K^\bullet=\varinjlim_i K_i^\bullet$ for the termwise colimit in module sheaves. For every $C\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map is an isomorphism of abelian groups:
$$
\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)}(C,K_i^\bullet[q])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)}(C,K^\bullet[q]).
$$

proof.text: Fix the diagram and colimit in the statement. By [det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-devissage], the objects $D$ for which $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(D,K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(D,K[q])$ is bijective for every $q$ form a class closed under shifts, isomorphisms and distinguished extensions. Clause (1), and only clause (1), of [det-lem-int-ext-formula] expresses $C$ as a finite extension of shifts of $a_!L$, with $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i$ closed and $u$ open, and $L\in\Cons(S,\mathcal O_E)$ locally the completion of a finitely generated module. It suffices to treat these pieces. All these schemes are in the standing finite-type setting, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (the base is a field). Opens are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and locally Noetherian schemes are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Thus $S,Z,X$ and $V=X\setminus Z$ are qcqs; in particular the complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: reduction by finite filtration; checking the standing qcqs hypotheses

proof.text:
Put $P=L^\vee:=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{E,S}}(L,\mathcal O_{E,S})$, the derived dual. Apply [det-lem-int-integral-heart-dualizable] with ambient scheme $S$, constructible sheaf $L$, and whole stratum $S$: $L$ is dualizable and $P$ has Tor amplitude $[0,1]$. Clause (1) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] gives $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$. The exact open-extension functor $u_!$ and its adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$ are [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]. The module pullbacks are exact and canonically naturally isomorphic to the lifts of inverse image by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Since an exact left adjoint has a right adjoint preserving K-injectives [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], the open adjunction also computes derived Hom. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K[q])=\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK[q])$. For any $M$, evaluation and coevaluation of the dual pair give inverse maps $\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\leftrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{E,S},P\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)$: send $f$ to $(1_P\otimes f)\circ\operatorname{coev}$, and send $g$ to $(\operatorname{ev}\otimes1_M)\circ(1_L\otimes g)$, with the symmetry and unit identifications understood. Their composites are identities by the two duality triangle identities. The derived monoidal structure is [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. The K-injective Hom comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] computes $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{E,S},N[q])$ by degree-$q$ cohomology of $\Gamma(S,I(N))$: a chain map from the coefficient unit in degree zero is a global cycle, and a homotopy changes it by a global boundary. By the definition of derived sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], this is $H^q(S,N)$. Apply this with $N=P\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$. We have therefore obtained, naturally in $K$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K[q])\cong H^q(S,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK).$$
This is clause (2) of the integral Hom-formula node in degree $q$, there written with the blueprint macro $\cHom=R\mathcal Hom$; it is derived here from the dualizability statement so that the dual is explicitly the derived dual, which for torsion $L$ (e.g. $L=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$, dual $\mathcal O_E/\pi_E[-1]$) differs from the underived sheaf Hom.

source.place: generator Hom formula, with the derived dual required by the integral-heart lemma

proof.text:
The hypotheses on the ambient category in the bounded-flat-model theorem hold as follows. Abelian sheaves are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the constant ring $\mathbf Z$, and their closed symmetric sheaf tensor is [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. For an abelian sheaf $M$ take the direct sum of free sheaves $\mathbf Z_U$ indexed by pairs $(U,s)$ with $s\in M(U)$; send its generator to $s$. This is a natural epimorphism, since every local section is in its image. Each $\mathbf Z_U$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat], taking $P=\mathbf Z$; tensor is right exact by closedness. Their direct sum is flat: tensor distributes over it, and direct sums of exact sequences are exact, being filtered colimits of finite subsums in the Grothendieck category. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] gives functorial flat resolutions of $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module objects. This module category is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and closed symmetric monoidal for the relative tensor by [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]; the tensor preserves colimits in each variable and hence is additive. Apply [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-flat-model] to $P$ in the closed monoidal category of $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module sheaves, with its relative tensor and K-flat derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Fix a flat complex $F=[F^0\to F^1]$ representing $P$. Its bounded flat terms make it K-flat: tensor with an acyclic complex is the cone of a map between acyclic complexes, so is acyclic. Define $T(B^\bullet)=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes u^*i^*B^\bullet)$, which represents $\Phi B:=P\otimes^{\mathbf L}u^*i^*B$. The pullbacks are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] and preserve colimits: the module pullback/pushforward adjunction is [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], so apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Each tensor $F^s\otimes-$ preserves colimits, since it is left adjoint to internal Hom [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom]. Explicitly $T(B)^n=(F^0\otimes u^*i^*B^n)\oplus(F^1\otimes u^*i^*B^{n-1})$, and the tensor differential is natural in $B$. Thus $\varinjlim_iT(B_i)=T(\varinjlim_iB_i)$ as complexes; if all $B_i$ vanish below $b$, so do all $T(B_i)$. Exactness and flatness show that $T$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Applying [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] to this actual bounded-below diagram on the qcqs scheme $S$ gives
$$\varinjlim_iH^q(S,\Phi K_i)\cong H^q(S,\Phi K).$$

source.place: finite Tor amplitude and continuity of the first fiber term

proof.text:
To handle the other fiber term, choose the functorial K-injective resolution $I(-)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence], available because module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Since $j^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $j_*$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] shows that applying $j_*$ termwise to $I(j^*K_i)$ and $I(j^*K)$ preserves K-injectivity, so these strict complexes compute $Rj_*j^*K_i$ and $Rj_*j^*K$. The complexes $A_i=j_*I(j^*K_i)$ and $A=j_*I(j^*K)$ and their cocone represent $Rj_*j^*K_i$ and $Rj_*j^*K$. These objects have cohomology zero below $b$: apply the quadrant and convergence assertions of [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to the left exact functor $j_*$ and $j^*K_i$ (respectively $j^*K$); every possible term in a total degree $<b$ is zero. Replace $A_i,A$ functorially by the quotients $J_i=A_i/\tau_{\le b-1}A_i$, $J=A/\tau_{\le b-1}A$ of the standard truncation subcomplexes [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Their only possibly nonzero terms are in degrees $\ge b-1$ (in degree $b-1$ the term $A^{b-1}/\ker d^{b-1}$), so they vanish termwise below $b-1$; the kernel $\tau_{\le b-1}A_i$ of $A_i\to J_i$ has cohomology $H^n(A_i)=0$ for $n\le b-1$, so $A_i\to J_i$ (and $A\to J$) is a quasi-isomorphism and $J_i,J$ represent the same derived objects. Exactness of module-sheaf filtered colimits [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives
$$H^r(\varinjlim_iJ_i)=\varinjlim_iH^r(J_i).$$
The qcqs direct-image theorem [det-lem-bounded-continuity-direct-image], applied to $j$ and the diagram $j^*K_i$, identifies the last sheaf with $H^r(J)$ for every $r$, because exact colimit-preserving $j^*$ identifies $\varinjlim_i j^*K_i$ with $j^*K$. Thus the cocone map $\varinjlim_iJ_i\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Step 3 now applies to $T(J_i)$, which have the common termwise lower bound $b-1$ (Step 3's bound argument holds for any integer): their colimit is $T(\varinjlim_iJ_i)$, and its map to $T(J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The sections theorem [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] therefore gives
$$\varinjlim_iH^q(S,\Phi Rj_*j^*K_i)\cong H^q(S,\Phi Rj_*j^*K).$$

source.place: continuity of the $Rj_*j^*$ term, using explicit bounded representatives

proof.text:
For each $B$, clause (3) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] supplies the natural fiber formula $R\underline\Gamma_ZB\simeq i^*\operatorname{fib}(B\to Rj_*j^*B)$. Exact pullbacks induce triangulated functors [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], tensor with the K-flat $F$ is triangulated [lem-sc-source-kflat-tensor-left-triangulated], and derived sections are triangulated [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Hence, putting $Q(B)=R\Gamma(S,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZB)$, $A(B)=R\Gamma(S,\Phi B)$ and $B'(B)=R\Gamma(S,\Phi Rj_*j^*B)$, there is a natural triangle $Q(B)\to A(B)\to B'(B)\to Q(B)[1]$. Notice that $u^*$, rather than $u^*i^*$, is applied to $R\underline\Gamma_ZB$, which already lives on $Z$. Its long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains
$$H^{q-1}A(K_i)\to H^{q-1}B'(K_i)\to H^qQ(K_i)\to H^qA(K_i)\to H^qB'(K_i).$$
Taking filtered colimits preserves exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. The cocone gives a commutative diagram from this exact row to the corresponding row for $K$. The first, second, fourth and fifth vertical arrows are isomorphisms by Steps 3 and 4. The five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes the middle arrow $\varinjlim_iH^qQ(K_i)\to H^qQ(K)$ an isomorphism.

source.place: fiber comparison and its explicit five-term exact rows

proof.text: The natural Hom identification constructed in Step 2 identifies the comparison in Step 5 with $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,K[q])$; every map was induced by the original colimit cocone. Thus each stratum piece belongs to the comparison class of Step 1. Apply its closure under shifts and distinguished extensions [det-lem-constructible-ext-continuity-devissage] successively along the finite filtration given by clause (1) of [det-lem-int-ext-formula]. The resulting comparison is the asserted isomorphism for $C$ in every degree $q$.

split_report.summary: Revalidated after the current DAG update to sk-def-sfb-derived-categories. The second reader derived the generator Hom formula directly from the existing derived-duality node (the blueprint's \cHom is its macro for the derived R\mathcal Hom, so the blueprint formula is not in error; the DAG text of det-lem-int-ext-formula leaves the macro unexpanded), made the standing scheme and coefficient setting explicit, and replaced the imprecise spectral-sequence comparison by a quasi-isomorphism between explicit bounded direct-image models and an explicit five-lemma diagram. No new nodes. Final sandbox audit supplied the flat-resolution hypotheses of the bounded flat model explicitly and declared the generic tools in split_report.tool_uses; the current derived-categories statement was reread and remains exactly the dependency used by the item statement.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the first filtration sentence; Step 2 realizes the generator Hom formula (clause (2) of det-lem-int-ext-formula, with the derived dual \cHom=R\mathcal Hom of the blueprint macro), derived from det-lem-int-integral-heart-dualizable; Steps 3 and 4 expand bounded continuity on the two fiber terms; Step 5 gives the fiber/five-lemma argument; Step 6 concludes. This is the unit route.

tool_uses.why: The comparison-class closure is the generic triangulated five-lemma argument for finite filtrations; it is used with integral generators supplied by this unit, not the field-only generation consequence.
Noetherian permanence checks the qcqs hypotheses on the strata in the prescribed filtration; it replaces no geometric step.
Noetherian open subschemes ensure that the complementary open and strata are quasi-compact.
Quasi-separatedness of the Noetherian strata is a general scheme tool needed by bounded continuity.
General qcqs permanence checks the complementary open immersion against the direct-image theorem.
A generic bounded flat representative realizes the derived dual of amplitude [0,1] as an actual complex, so the existing continuity theorem with a termwise lower bound applies.
Generic K-flat tensor triangulatedness allows the prescribed closed-support fiber triangle to be tensored with the derived dual.
Free abelian sheaves on site objects provide the functorial flat epimorphism required to apply the existing module-object flat-resolution theorem.
Generic inheritance of functorial flat resolutions supplies a hypothesis of the bounded-flat-model theorem for the relative module tensor.
General ringed-site AB5 and Grothendieck structure provide exact filtered sheaf colimits and the hypothesis for functorial K-injective resolutions.
Functorial resolutions realize the direct-image comparison by one strict diagram of complexes, with no alternative geometric argument.
The generic adjoint lemma justifies deriving the exact open adjunction in the generator Hom calculation.
The generic localization bijection identifies maps from the coefficient unit with global cycles modulo boundaries.
Generic adjoint colimit preservation gives termwise pullback/tensor compatibility with the original cocone.
Generic right-derived triangulatedness supplies the triangle of derived sections in the unit fiber argument.
The generic long exact cohomology sequence gives the displayed five consecutive terms of that fiber triangle.
Generic exact-functor triangulatedness applies the exact coefficient pullbacks to that same fiber triangle.
Exact filtered colimits in abelian groups preserve the displayed long exact rows.
The five lemma is the formal comparison step for the fiber triangle, as required by the unit route.
Only the quadrant and convergence clauses of the generic bounded-below hypercohomology spectral sequence prove that Rj_* preserves the lower cohomological bound.
